name: OpenAI Codex CLI
disclaimer: Written from documented interface, not verified against an install. Flags drift; correct and open a PR.

stdin.note: Verified from the command reference (learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands, surface cli), read 2026-09-17: codex exec takes PROMPT as `string | - (read stdin)`, and `-` pipes the prompt from stdin.
Verified from the same reference: codex exec resume takes its PROMPT as `string | - (read stdin)` too.

options.trust_none_why: codex exec keeps its shell tool; --sandbox read-only limits it but does not remove it
options.sandbox_note: codex exec takes --sandbox and codex exec resume does not (openai/codex issue 40149); a resume takes -c sandbox_mode="<mode>", which every exec subcommand accepts.

--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandb.why: No documented combination runs an unattended implementer's loop without it. codex exec asks nobody - it answers every approval with never - and runs in a read-only sandbox unless told otherwise. Its workspace-write sandbox (-c sandbox_mode="workspace-write" after exec resume; --full-auto is gone since 0.147.0) keeps <writable_root>/.git read-only and the network off, so an implementer could edit and test but never stage, commit or run its reviewer. The watchdog starts no turn with it until a person names codex in watchdog.bypass_adapters on this machine, and ao doctor names what that allows. Read on 2026-09-17 from learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sandboxing, /docs/non-interactive-mode, /docs/developer-commands and /docs/config-file/config-reference, and github.com/openai/codex (codex-rs/exec/src/cli.rs; issues 40149 and 7071).
